slot.topic_title: Setting Up a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Means

item.title: Is a Two-Sample t-Test Appropriate? Onboarding Setup Times
item.stimulus: A software company believes its new onboarding process reduces the mean time customers need to finish setup. Thousands of customers use each process. The company independently and randomly selected 36 customers who used the new process (sample mean 21.4 minutes) and 14 customers who used the standard process (sample mean 26.8 minutes). A dotplot of the 36 new-process times has no strong skewness and no outliers. A dotplot of the 14 standard-process times is skewed right with one outlier.

parts.prompt: Let μ₁ be the mean for the new onboarding process and μ₂ the mean for the standard process. Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean setup time, in minutes, of all customers who use the new onboarding process, and μ₂ is the true mean setup time of all customers who use the standard process.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean setup time, in minutes, of all customers who use the new onboarding process, and μ₂ is the true mean setup time of all customers who use the standard process, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ < 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ < 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure, and decide whether its conditions are met. Justify each decision.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the customers were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of customers.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the customers were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of customers.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of customers in its group.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of customers in its group.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: one sample (n = 14) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the standard-process sample has an outlier and is skewed, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition, says whether it is met, and gives the reason: one sample (n = 14) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the standard-process sample has an outlier and is skewed, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean setup time, in minutes, of all customers who use the new onboarding process, and μ₂ is the true mean setup time of all customers who use the standard process. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ < 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means. Randomization: the customers were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of customers. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of customers in its group. Sample-data condition: one sample (n = 14) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the standard-process sample has an outlier and is skewed, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
item.verification_python:
n1, n2 = 36, 14
both_big = min(n1, n2) >= 30
assert both_big == False
assert 21.4 < 26.8
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
